briefs.body:
Five handling facts live only inside plan reports and have no row in Working/Translation/T_ROWS.jsonl: the flip idle timer, four-wheel drive, the spin-in-place gate (21.6 km/h), the battle yaw-toward-aim members (BattleModeSteerAngleFactor, BattleModeMaxSteering 80, BattleModeStopAndTurnAngleMoving 90, YawOffset 0), and the water and remote entries. Read tmp/freebuff/reports/bm-moving-yaw-toward-aim.md, four-wheel-drive-and-spin-in-place-build-plan.md, stuck-flip-build-plan-merge.md and flip-recovery-idle-timer-and-thruster-plan.md. For each fact write one proposed ledger row in the exact field layout of the existing rows: id, BmAK value with its offset in Research/BatmobileGrab/BMSDK_OFFSETS.json, JC3 carrier, class (decoded, derived or assumed), verify cell, pursuit or battle. Write the proposals to Working/Translation/HDL_ROW_PROPOSALS.jsonl and do NOT edit T_ROWS.jsonl, since the apply chain owns it. Done check: every proposed row parses as JSON and every cited offset is found in the offsets file by a script you run and quote. Mark anything not found as UNKNOWN. Battle-mode rows are tagged for the modes landmark.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

After brief 7964 reports which stuck timer is read, settle the remaining handling members the plans still call UNKNOWN. Take three members: BattleModeSteerBiasRate (who consumes it), the four AirControl* members (where the airborne window of 1.211 s comes from), and the leftover Batmobile stuck/flip pair if 7964 left either open. Inputs: Research/BatmobileGrab/BMSDK_OFFSETS.json, the cooked class defaults under Research/BatmobileGrab/, Research/BatmobileGrab/DRIVE_MODES.md and MECHANICS.md. For each member classify it as serialised (a value sits in a cooked file, cite file and byte), declared (class default only) or exe-only (read by native code, no data evidence), and write a one-line 5-minute experiment that would settle each exe-only one. Output tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-unknown-members-walk.md as a table with columns member, offset, class, evidence path, experiment. Done check: no row has an empty evidence cell, and the count of members walked is printed. Do not infer any value from memory of the real game.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Settle task T-26: the three drag members of the Arkham Knight Batmobile sim, Drag at offset 16, DragNoLoad at offset 20 and DriftDrag at offset 712 (Research/BatmobileGrab/BMSDK_OFFSETS.json). Question: are their values stored in the cooked class default or sub-object bytes, or only set by native code? Method: locate the cooked Batmobile vehicle sim default object using Tools/scripts/upk_read.py and Research/BatmobileGrab/CLASS_DEFAULTS.md, then walk its tagged property list for those three names and for every float property in the aerodynamic or speed-limit family. Print each hit with file, byte offset and value; print an explicit not-serialised line for each miss. The ledger rows T-R2 and T-A2 currently keep drag at the class fit because this is unsettled. Write tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-drag-triple.md with a verdict per member (serialised value, declared only, exe-only) and what that does to the 267 km/h terminal-speed prediction in Working/Q/PREDICTIONS.md D-2. Read-only. Done check: re-run the walk script twice and show identical output.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Rows T-R1 (arcade friction 1.0 to 3.0) and T-G5 (wheel friction_type 0 to 2) each rest on a single probe, not on a range. Build the census that gives them a domain. Use Tools/scripts/jc3fleet.py and the vehicle module data under Research/JC3Grab/ to list, for every land vehicle in the fleet, the wheel and tyre grip members: friction_type, arcade friction, slip values, handbrake friction factor and any lateral grip scale. Output Research/JC3Grab/GRIP_CENSUS.json plus a short GRIP_CENSUS.md giving per member the min, max, median, the donor car (Serpente, entity v0300 sportsmuscle debug) value, and which vehicles sit above 3.0. State for T-R1 and T-G5 whether the proposed value is inside, at the edge of, or beyond the fleet range, and what that predicts for tyre behaviour. Done check: the JSON vehicle count equals the fleet count printed by jc3fleet.py, and the script is rerunnable with --check giving the same hash. Report-only on game data; no edits to any Builds tree.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Close the open items of GRAB task G3-01b on the Arkham Knight collision asset. Open: rotations of the three boxes of Physics.Batmobile_V3_Physics, what the packed byte at 0x4C of each FKBoxElem means (read tmp/freebuff/reports/box-flag-0x4c-witness.md, do not redo it), the extents convention (full length or half length), and which mesh is active per mode. Inputs: Research/BatmobileGrab/COLLISION_GEOM.md, COLLISION_WHERE.md, COLLISION_FRAME.md, COLLISION_SELECTOR2.md and the cooked physics file named there. Decode each box transform as centre, quaternion and extents, then convert to the JC3 frame already used in Working/Collision2/bm_vehicle_hull.json. State the convention as proven by comparing your decoded chassis box with the 690.305 x 374.536 x 207.5 cm figures already in Working/Translation/T22_REOPEN.md; if the two disagree by a factor two, that is the answer. Write Research/BatmobileGrab/COLLISION_GEOM2.md. Done check: all three boxes list centre, rotation and extents with the byte offset each came from; anything unproven is marked UNKNOWN.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Finish GRAB task G3-06f: the 17 interaction, threat and physics component objects of the Batmobile package (one of them a CylinderComponent) that the remainder accounting listed but never opened. Start from Research/BatmobileGrab/REMAINDER.md and NATIVE_TRIAGE.md to get the object names and export indices, then decode each: class, owner, key properties, and whether it influences driving (grip zone, damage zone, pick-up trigger, sensor volume) or is unrelated. For the CylinderComponent give radius, height and the transform in the same frame as COLLISION_FRAME.md. Put results in Research/BatmobileGrab/INTERACTION_COMPONENTS.md and a machine file INTERACTION_COMPONENTS.json. For each driving-relevant one name the closest JC3 system and the gap, never writing that JC3 has no system. Done check: 17 of 17 objects appear in the JSON, each with a classification and a byte-level evidence path; a count line is printed by a small checker script you also commit under Tools/scripts/.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

The earlier intent of decoding the handling, upright, damage and material classes of the Batmobile package was never delivered; Research/BatmobileGrab/REMAINDER.md only accounts for bytes. Close it. Using Research/BatmobileGrab/REMAINDER_SAMPLE_AUDIT.md for the sample list, pick every object whose class name mentions upright, stuck, flip, damage, health, surface or material, and decode its tagged properties with Tools/scripts/upk_read.py. Produce Research/BatmobileGrab/HANDLING_CLASSES.md with one section per class: purpose, property table with values, which pursuit-handling ledger row it feeds (for example T-SR1 self-right or T-DM7 contact damage), and whether the value is serialised or exe-only. Cross-check the stuck and flip values against BatmobileStuckTimeMax 2.0 s and BatmobileStuckTimeFlip 0.5 s in the offsets file and say which object the numbers really sit in. Done check: every object found is listed once; a final line gives counts of serialised versus exe-only properties; unresolved items are named UNKNOWN with a 5-minute experiment.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Brief 7976 built Tools/scripts/bmak_live_read.py for the GOG Arkham Knight copy and brief 7989 listed six values it will print. Extend the reader so one run also captures every pursuit-handling number this landmark still lacks. Add to its offset table, each validated by its existing --check against the two grab JSONs: the engine torque and rpm members, the steering curves StandardSteeringSpeedCurve, BoostSteeringSpeedCurve and HandbrakeSteeringSpeedCurve, SteeringReductionFactor and SteeringReductionSpeed, the three drag members (use hdl-03 for which are plausible), the speed cap members, DriftDrag and drift torque, the brake and handbrake members, suspension length and travel, and the boost members (BoostDuration, cooldowns). Operator fact: how steering behaves at speed is unknown to the operator, so the steering curves are priority one. Keep the reader strictly read-only: no WriteProcessMemory. Run python Tools/scripts/bmak_live_read.py --check and --selftest and paste the outputs. Output a field list in tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-reader-handling-fields.md giving each field's offset, type and the ledger row it will fill.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Supervised read-only session on the GOG Arkham Knight copy at E:/Games/BmAK-GOG-sdk (not JC3). Operator drives; the agent runs the extended reader. Pilot cards: Working/Q/PILOT/LAUNCH.md and KILL.md adapted in the report you write first; kill only by exact PID. Steps: start the game, spawn the Batmobile on a flat road, run python Tools/scripts/bmak_live_read.py --json into Working/Q/bmak_live/ at rest, then while the operator accelerates in a straight line to top speed (afterburner off, then held), brakes hard from 100 mph, holds full steering lock at low speed and at high speed, and handbrakes into a turn, record the reader output once per second to the same folder. Also ask the operator for a 20-second screen recording of: roof-rest until the thrusters fire (stopwatch visible), and a standstill stick-spin. Pass rule: the file holds the six values from 7989 plus the new handling fields, or each missing one carries a stated reason. Fail route: write the reader error and stop; do not guess values. The observation is the JSON file, not a screenshot.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Take the JSON files and the operator footage that hdl-09 saved under Working/Q/bmak_live/ and turn them into handling targets. Write a new file Working/Q/HDL_TARGETS.md with targets for: A1 0-100, A2 top speed with and without boost, A5 braking distance from 100 mph, A3 turn radius at 60 and 100 km/h, A4 lock time, A9 boost acceleration, and flip-recovery delay. Each target gets a value, the unit, how it was obtained (live memory read, footage frame count, or derived) and the class (measured, decoded, derived, assumed). Where hdl-09 measured something it replaces the old assumed value: list old value, new value and the ledger row it moves (T-E5, T-M1, T-K1, T-ST1, T-ST7, T-SR1 and others). Do not edit T_ROWS.jsonl; write proposed edits to Working/Translation/HDL_TARGET_ROW_EDITS.jsonl. Done check: every target row has class and source; the 336 km/h label stays assumed unless a measurement supersedes it. Anything still empty stays UNKNOWN, with the missing capture named.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Brief 7982 writes a per-second JSON-lines telemetry file (%LOCALAPPDATA%/jc3-batmobile-hook/telemetry.jsonl: time, position, rotation, speed, health), and 7983 logs the gamepad stick state. Build the offline analyser that replaces screenshots for driving takes. Write Tools/scripts/telemetry_takes.py with one sub-command per take: launch (0-100 km/h time and distance, A1), topspeed (peak and plateau, A2), brake (100-0 distance and mean deceleration, A5), boost (0-100 with boost, m/s^2, A9), corner (radius = speed over yaw rate from successive headings, A3), lock (time from stick full deflection to yaw-rate onset, A4, flagged coarse if the log rate is below 10 Hz), drift (peak slip angle and recovery time, A7), landing (height channel from position z, rebound count, A6). Every output line carries the band from Working/Q/PREDICTIONS.md. If a channel is missing from the 7982 schema, print UNKNOWN with the field name; never interpolate. Done check: --help lists all eight; running with no file prints the expected path and exits 2.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Prove Tools/scripts/telemetry_takes.py against data whose answers are known before it runs. Write Tools/scripts/telemetry_synth.py that generates eight synthetic telemetry.jsonl files in Working/Q/synth/ in the 7982 schema: constant-acceleration launch to 100 km/h in exactly 16.4 s, a plateau at 267 km/h, a braking run with deceleration 3.65 m/s^2, a circle of 13.82 m radius at 100 km/h, a step steer with lock at 0.25 s, a landing with two rebounds, and two files with a channel deliberately removed. Run each sub-command and compare to the known answer; the tolerance is one sample interval. Also feed it a file sampled at 1 Hz and confirm the lock sub-command refuses to give a number. Write the comparison table to tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-verify-analyser.md. Done check: all eight cases pass, the two missing-channel cases print UNKNOWN, the coarse-rate case prints a refusal, and the script exits 0 only when all pass.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Tools/scripts/v05_driving.py has six predicted checks D-1 to D-6 and none for take A9 (0-100 with boost, a pilot band of 6.00 m/s^2 plus or minus 25 percent from tmp/freebuff/reports/pilot-card-driving-takes.md section 5.5). Add a D-7 row. Derive the boost prediction from the ledger rows T-B1 (torque multiplier 6.3), T-B2 (extra top speed 43.2 km/h), T-B3 (grip 1.0) and T-E2, reading every number from Working/Translation/T_ROWS.jsonl rather than typing it. Regenerate Working/Q/PREDICTIONS.md with the script's --write and confirm --check is byte-identical on a second run. Also change the heading count text so it says seven checks. Record in the report which row classes are measured, derived or assumed for D-7. Output tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-v05-a9-row.md. Done check: python Tools/scripts/v05_driving.py --check exits 0 and prints a D-7 line; revert is a git checkout of the two files.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Write the explicit four-wheel-drive decision for the Batmobile. Facts: Research/JC3Grab/DRIVE_CARRIERS.md found steering_type with FrontSteered on 51 vehicles and absent on 3, no rear or all-wheel enum, one driveline. The project rule is that the answer is never that JC3 has no system; name the closest one and the gap. Read tmp/freebuff/reports/four-wheel-drive-and-spin-in-place-build-plan.md and the output of brief 9122 (tmp/freebuff/reports/rc5-drive-modes-and-yaw.md). Produce tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-four-wheel-drive-decision.md: the composition chosen (for example per-axle grip and slip asymmetry plus the drift yaw block), each member with its value and class, the predicted behavioural difference from a front-steered car, the residual gap in one sentence, and the take that will test it (name the card and the one observation). Done check: the decision lists at least three members, each is looked up in Working/Translation/T1_TRANSLATION.md and found, and anything not found is marked UNKNOWN.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Two battle-adjacent handling rows are marked blocked: T-MD8 (turn on the spot, no data carrier per Research/JC3Grab/TANKTURN.md) and the two slip scales of T-MD7 that have no member. Battle mode ownership sits with the modes landmark (brief mod-01); this brief only delivers the handling-side composition that mode work consumes. Read tmp/freebuff/reports/tank-pivot-values-for-battle-mode-turn-plan.md, tank-pivot-donor-trace.md and drive-mode-torque-arithmetic-substitute-plan.md. For each unmatched item name the closest JC3 system (candidates: drift yaw torque, a differential-style left-right drive split, the bike-style lean carriers, an authored script graph), the value to write, and the gap that remains. Write tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-pivot-slip-composition.md with a table: item, closest system, members and values, predicted yaw rate in deg/s, gap, test card. Done check: no cell says unsupported; every predicted yaw rate shows its arithmetic; UNKNOWN items point to a 5-minute experiment.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Re-derive a legitimate lever set for top speed. Known: the build's drag class fit Cd 0.55 predicts 267 km/h terminal (Working/Q/PREDICTIONS.md D-2), boost adds 32.4-43.2 km/h, and the 336.4 km/h (209 mph) label is assumed (tmp/freebuff/reports/correction-8391-top-speed-label.md); no back-solved drag may be used. Lore accuracy wins, so the target is to reach the label with levers that are individually justified. Using hdl-03 (what the drag triple really is) compute terminal speed for each lever alone and in combination: final drive and gear ratio (T-E4), rpm band top (T-E1), torque (T-E2), boost thrust (T-B1/B2) and the speed cap member, with the physics shown. Choose one set that reaches 300-336 km/h with boost and mark each value as lore (decoded), derived or tune. Output tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-top-speed-levers.md plus the set as a JSON file Working/Translation/HDL_TOPSPEED_SET.json. Done check: a script recomputes the terminal speeds from the JSON and prints them to match the report; do not ask the operator a compromise question, record the choice and its class.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Generate one ledger of every per-mode handling value so the mode pair build has a single source. Inputs: Research/BatmobileGrab/MODES.md, DRIVE_MODES.md, the variant tables written by briefs 9121 (suspension stiffness 3000 and 750, damping 300 and 20, bias 50, 10, 5) and 9122 (drive and steering variants), and the handling cells of 9120. Write Tools/scripts/mode_value_table.py (--write, --check) that outputs Working/Translation/MODE_VALUE_TABLE.json and .md with one row per member: name, pursuit value, battle value, the JC3 member that carries it, class, owner brief, and status (built, planned, gap). Include the 600 cm/s turning-mode speed cap and BattleModeVSpeedCurve points. Rows whose battle value belongs to another landmark carry the tag modes and are listed, not decided. Done check: --check passes twice with identical hashes, and a count line gives rows by status; every gap row carries the card that closes it.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Pursuit mode rule from the plans: with the car slow, the left stick spins it in place, and above a gate of 21.6 km/h normal steering takes over; JC3 gives a drift yaw block instead. Compute the predicted behaviour so a pilot take has a band. From tmp/freebuff/reports/four-wheel-drive-and-spin-in-place-build-plan.md milestone M1 and the cells built by 9122 (tmp/freebuff/reports/rc5-drive-modes-and-yaw.md) derive: yaw rate at standstill in deg/s, speed at which spin hands over to steering, and the stopping time of the spin after the stick is released. Store them in Working/Q/HDL_SPIN_PREDICTION.json with formula, inputs and a plus or minus band, plus one pilot-card sentence. Where an input is UNKNOWN, say which, and write the single measurement that would fix it. Done check: a script recomputes every value from the JSON inputs and prints identical numbers; the file passes a JSON parse; the operator-unknown parts are labelled and not guessed.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Operator fact: the Arkham Knight Batmobile takes no crash damage. Row T-DM7 (contact damage speed band) must therefore be reconciled with that fact. Read the row in Working/Translation/T_ROWS.jsonl, Research/BatmobileGrab/HANDLING_CLASSES.md from hdl-07 if it exists, tmp/freebuff/reports/audit-ram-assist-plan-numbers.md and the JC3 vehicle damage module members (collision damage multiplier, damage-per-impact, explosion-on-death) located through Tools/scripts/jc3fleet.py. Decide the cell set that makes collisions with walls, kerbs, traffic and ramming deal zero damage to the player car while ram assist still hurts the target as T-RA1 requires. Cite each member by module path and current Serpente value. Output tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-no-crash-damage-plan.md with a before and after table and the reverse step. Done check: every proposed cell is found in the module data by a script that prints path and value; risks to traffic and AI cars sharing the module are named explicitly.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Create the tyre grip branch as its own tree so tyre retunes never touch the handling merge. From Builds/bm-RC5-handling's scaffold pattern (see tmp/freebuff/reports/rc5-handling-values.md) write Tools/scripts/rc5_grip.py (--write, --check) producing Builds/bm-RC5-grip with exactly these cells: arcade friction (T-R1, target 3.0), wheel friction_type (T-G5, target 2) and the slip pair 0.1 and 0.05 (T-S5), after comparing each against the census range of Research/JC3Grab/GRIP_CENSUS.md from hdl-04. Include a tuning table at the top of the script mapping each cell to the takes it moves (A3 radius, A4 lock time, A5 braking, A7 drift) so that later fix iterations change one number from one place. Register the branch under Working/RC5/branches/ using the format of reports/rc5-scaffold-and-merge-script.md. Never edit any bm-RC4 tree or the game folder. Done check: --check reads every cell back through the built .toc slice and prints the three values; any clamp is recorded.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Independent read-back of Builds/bm-RC5-grip. Do not trust rc5_grip.py's own --check; open the built module through the .toc with the generic reader used by Tools/scripts/t_rows.py and print arcade friction, friction_type and the slip pair, then diff the entire module against its source donor and list every changed byte range. Expect only the three intended cells to differ; any other difference is a fail with the offset shown. Confirm the branch record exists under Working/RC5/branches/ and that its declared cells equal what you found. Check also that no other branch record (handling, suspension, drive) declares the same module path, and list overlaps for the merge step. Write tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-verify-grip.md with PASS or FAIL per cell and the diff summary. Done check: byte-range count equals the declared cell count; the report states the revert step, which is deleting Builds/bm-RC5-grip and its branch record.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Build the afterburner glue as branch Builds/bm-RC5-boost with Tools/scripts/rc5_boost.py (--write, --check). Cells: boost duration 2.0 s, the quick-recharge cooldowns, the boost-to-drift interaction (DriftingBoostCooldown 1.5 s) and heat_boost restore (T-B4), using the nitro_boost block already set by 9120 (torque multiplier 6.3, grip 1.5, extra 80) as the base so you add and do not repeat. Source the BmAK values from Research/BatmobileGrab/MODES.md and the walk report tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-unknown-members-walk.md; where that report says exe-only, write the cell as assumed in the branch record, with the class stated. Share the effects half (flames, sound) with the weapons landmark by writing only the physics cells. Put a tuning table at the top mapping each cell to takes A2 and A9. Register the branch under Working/RC5/branches/ in the standard format. Done check: --check reads each cell back through the .toc and prints it next to its ledger row id.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Check Builds/bm-RC5-boost from outside its own script. Parse the built nitro or boost module via the .toc, print every cell hdl-22 claims, and compare them with ledger rows T-B1 to T-B4 in Working/Translation/T_ROWS.jsonl and with Research/BatmobileGrab/MODES.md. Then compute the predicted boosted launch acceleration and the boosted terminal-speed gain and confirm they land inside the D-2b band (32.4 to 43.2 km/h) and the A9 band of 6.00 m/s^2 plus or minus 25 percent; if either leaves its band report the cell that causes it. Check that the 9120 cells were not overwritten (diff against Builds/bm-RC5-handling). Write tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-verify-boost.md. Done check: PASS or FAIL per cell, plus a line for each band; the branch record is present; revert is removal of the tree and branch record.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Build the top-speed lever set chosen by brief hdl-16 (Working/Translation/HDL_TOPSPEED_SET.json) as a private branch: Builds/bm-RC5-topspeed with Tools/scripts/rc5_topspeed.py (--write, --check). Write the final-drive or gear ratio cells (T-E4, five gears with the first shift at 67 km/h as measured in QA-1), the rpm band cells (T-E1: 800, 2800, 4500) as needed, the speed cap member and any torque change the set chooses. Each cell carries its class from the JSON (lore, derived, tune) into the branch record so release notes can list them. Do not edit drag away from the class fit unless the JSON says so. Include a tuning table at the head of the script mapping every cell to takes A1 and A2. Register under Working/RC5/branches/. Done check: --check reads every cell back through the .toc and recomputes the terminal-speed prediction from the built numbers, matching the JSON to within 1 km/h.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Verify the Builds/bm-RC5-topspeed tree independently. Read each changed cell through the .toc, diff the module against the donor, and ensure only the cells listed in Working/Translation/HDL_TOPSPEED_SET.json differ. Recompute terminal speed with a fresh script not reusing rc5_topspeed.py: P = torque x wash x omega, v = (2P over rho Cd A) to the one third, with the built numbers, and compare with the A2 bands 240-294 km/h boost off and the delta band 32.4-43.2 km/h; also report the first-shift speed from the gear table against the 67 km/h measurement. If the new set predicts a value outside those old bands, say that the bands need regenerating (v05_driving.py) and give the new values; do not edit them. Write tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-verify-topspeed.md. Done check: PASS or FAIL per cell and per prediction; overlap with the handling and grip branch module paths is listed for the merge brief.
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Build the plan of tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-no-crash-damage-plan.md as branch Builds/bm-RC5-damage with Tools/scripts/rc5_damage.py (--write, --check). Operator fact: the Batmobile takes no crash damage; ram assist must still harm other vehicles. Write only the cells the plan lists in the vehicle damage module, leaving traffic and AI cars on their own modules untouched (check how the entity references its module so a shared module does not leak the change to other cars; if it does leak, build a private copy and say so). Put a tuning table at the top mapping each cell to the collision take. Register under Working/RC5/branches/ in the standard format. Never edit bm-RC4 trees or the game folder. Done check: --check reads each cell back through the .toc, prints module path, old and new value, and a final line stating how many other entities reference the same module path (found by a search of the entity list).
Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Verify Builds/bm-RC5-damage without using rc5_damage.py. Read the changed module through the .toc, diff against its donor, list every changed byte range, and confirm that only the cells named in the plan differ. Then search every entity in the shipped fleet for the module path and print the entities that would inherit the change; the expected answer is only the Batmobile entity, anything else is a fail that must be turned into a private-module card. Confirm that the damage values interact correctly with ram assist of brief 9123 (Builds/bm-RC5-movement): the ram damage written there must target other vehicles and must not be zeroed by this branch. Write tmp/freebuff/reports/hdl-verify-damage.md with PASS or FAIL for cells, leakage and ram interplay. Done check: leakage list is printed even when empty; revert is deleting the tree and branch record.
